strengths: The paper develops a clear and potentially valuable connection between GPTQ-style successive interference cancellation and classical reverse-waterfilling. Under its Gaussian-weight, high-rate, and large-layer assumptions, the AM–GM analysis gives an intuitive reason to use unequal per-column spacings and predicts a 0.255-bit scalar-quantization gap.

The empirical results are promising: WaterSIC improves the perplexity–rate frontier across Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, and Qwen3-8B, with especially large improvements over entropy-coded GPTQ below three bits. The downstream evaluations generally support that these gains are not confined to WikiText-2 perplexity.

The manuscript supplies extensive algorithmic details, calibration procedures, hyperparameters, per-layer mixing coefficients, codec diagnostics, and component-level MSE ablations. It also candidly identifies the lack of inference-throughput measurements and evaluation on very large models as limitations.

The unequal-rate allocation appears original in this PTQ setting, while the combination with activation-drift correction, residual compensation, attention weighting, and adaptive mixing is practically substantive. No material research-ethics concern is evident, although the impact statement is generic.
weaknesses: The headline near-optimality claim is materially broader than the theorem. The 0.255-bit result is only an iterated asymptotic limit as distortion tends to zero and the number of output rows tends to infinity, for iid Gaussian weights and an ideal entropy code. It does not establish near-optimality for finite-rate real LLM weights, including the practically important 1–4-bit regime emphasized in the abstract.

Theorem 3.3 is stated for every positive-semidefinite covariance, but the derivation requires positive Cholesky diagonals, divides by those diagonals, and invokes the high-rate identity only when distortion is below every positive eigenvalue. Singular PSD matrices therefore invalidate the stated formula. Related formal inconsistencies include an unnormalized definition of rate despite later using bits per dimension, an incorrect reconstruction transform in Section 3.1, and type-inconsistent translation identities in Appendix A. These issues make the central theoretical statement unreliable as written rather than merely cosmetically imprecise.

The reported rates are not fully operational or uniformly comparable. Main results use empirical symbol entropy plus scale overhead, whereas several baselines use log-cardinality. Actual Zstandard/LZMA sizes are shown only for two layers and exceed entropy by roughly 0.04–0.20 bits/weight; full-model bitstreams, entropy-model metadata, and decoder storage are not measured. Consequently, the claim of a state-of-the-art frontier at matched compressed size is not conclusively demonstrated.

The experiments do not isolate whether end-task gains arise from unequal rate allocation—the stated key innovation—or from the many additional corrections. The component ablations report layer-input MSE, mostly at four bits, rather than perplexity or downstream accuracy. A controlled full-model comparison of PlainWaterSIC versus equal-spacing Huffman-GPTQ with all other corrections held fixed is needed.

The Qwen3-8B pipeline manually zeros four architecture-specific outlier rows in both the reference and quantized model, substantially improving quantization stability, while baselines are imported from prior work on the original model. Showing that unquantized perplexity changes by less than 0.01 does not establish that this intervention is fair to competing quantizers; an ablation and application of the same preprocessing to baselines are required.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the detailed appendix: no code or executable bitstream format is provided, and model revisions, software environment, random seeds, benchmark harness/settings, rescaler stopping parameters, and several codec details are unspecified. strengths: The core idea is original and intuitively well motivated: assigning different quantization spacings to input channels connects GPTQ-style successive interference cancellation with classical waterfilling. The Cholesky-diagonal prescription is simple and potentially useful.
The manuscript attempts a meaningful theoretical comparison between entropy-coded GPTQ and PlainWaterSIC, identifying an AM–GM penalty for uniform grid spacing under an i.i.d. Gaussian weight model.

Reported results are promising across Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.2-1B, and Qwen3-8B. WaterSIC generally improves perplexity over Huffman-GPTQ, with particularly large gains near two bits, and the appendix includes zero-shot evaluations, compression-codec measurements, and layerwise diagnostics.

The paper openly acknowledges important practical limitations, including the absence of end-to-end decompression/inference benchmarks, dependence on layerwise Euclidean objectives, and evaluation only up to 8B models. No major application-level ethical concern is apparent.
weaknesses: The central 0.255-bit guarantee is substantially overstated. The theorem is a sequential asymptotic result requiring infinitely many output rows and vanishing distortion/high rate under the Gaussian-weight model. It does not establish a uniform finite-rate guarantee at the evaluated 1–4-bit regime, for real LLM weights, or for the full WaterSIC algorithm containing drift correction, adaptive mixing, rescaling, and other heuristics. Nevertheless, the abstract and introduction present the result as uniformly applying to all covariance matrices and as evidence of practical near-optimality.

The theoretical statement is not valid as written for every positive-semidefinite covariance matrix. Singular matrices can have zero Cholesky diagonals and determinant zero, making the proposed spacings and high-rate determinant expressions undefined; moreover, the all-active high-rate waterfilling formula assumes strictly positive eigenvalues. Near-singular cases also undermine any claimed uniformity.

The proof contains a serious sign inconsistency in its entropy asymptotics. Equations (41), (42), and (57) assert a finite limit for H(Z)-log(alpha), whereas high-resolution quantization gives H(Z)+log(alpha) approaching differential entropy as alpha tends to zero. The manuscript later uses the latter scaling implicitly to obtain a finite rate–distortion limit. Thus, the displayed proof does not establish Theorem 3.3 as written. Rate is also defined as total expected code length but subsequently treated as bits per dimension, without the necessary normalization.

The empirical comparison does not use a common storage or execution model. WaterSIC is primarily charged empirical entropy, while several baselines are charged log-cardinality; actual Zstandard/LZMA rates are only checked on a handful of layers and exceed entropy. No complete compressed-model size, decoder metadata accounting, decoding throughput, memory bandwidth, latency, or executable low-precision kernel is evaluated. Consequently, the broad practical SOTA claim is not adequately supported.

There is problematic test-set use in the Qwen3-8B protocol: the authors manually zero selected rows and justify that decision by checking that it changes WikiText-2 test perplexity by less than 0.01. Using the reported test set to choose model preprocessing compromises the independence of the main Qwen evaluation.

The ablations do not isolate the contribution of unequal rate allocation to end-task performance. Most component ablations show layerwise relative MSE at a single rate, while the final system combines several existing or heuristic techniques. There is no perplexity ablation progressing from Huffman-GPTQ to PlainWaterSIC and then through every full-system component, making the source of the reported gains unclear.

Reproducibility is inadequate for such a complicated and expensive pipeline. No code or complete compressed artifacts are provided; random seeds, sampled calibration rows, rescaler tolerance/ridge/iteration settings, precise software versions, and full baseline procedures are missing. Algorithm 3 also uses undefined or inconsistent indices (for example, z_k and gamma_k inside an i-loop), preventing direct implementation. There are no repeated runs or uncertainty estimates.

The experimental scope is strongly centered on WikiText-2, which is used for full-split calibration, model-specific tuning, and primary evaluation. Some baselines are imported from prior work while others are rerun under different rate conventions and configurations. The limited independent datasets and inconsistent baseline protocols weaken the generality of the evidence.

The limitations discussion is honest about hardware throughput and model scale, but omits the more consequential limitations of the asymptotic theory, Gaussian-weight assumption, incompatible rate accounting, extensive calibration/search cost, manual model surgery, and test-set-informed preprocessing. Overall, the promising idea and results do not outweigh the unresolved central soundness, evaluation, and reproducibility problems.

strengths: Soundness: The core theoretical argument is compelling. The paper relates GPTQ to successive interference cancellation, identifies the AM-GM penalty induced by uniform column spacings, and derives waterfilling-inspired spacings. Theorem 3.3 establishes an asymptotic gap of 0.5 log2(2πe/12), approximately 0.255 bits, while also explaining why GPTQ's gap can grow with heterogeneous Cholesky diagonals.

Significance: The resulting rate-perplexity improvements are substantial, particularly at low rates. For example, WaterSIC obtains perplexity 16.19 at 2.00 bits on Llama-3.2-1B versus QTIP's 18.67 at 2.02 bits, and 11.37 at 2.125 bits on Qwen3-8B versus Huffman-GPTQ's 13.97. Similar improvements are reported on Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B.

Originality: Per-input-channel rate allocation derived from classical reverse waterfilling is a simple but insightful departure from uniform-rate GPTQ-style quantization. The paper offers useful new understanding of an established method rather than merely adding another quantization heuristic.

Evaluation: Results cover four model families/sizes, rates from roughly 1 to 4 bits, WikiText-2 perplexity, KL divergence, and multiple zero-shot tasks. The appendices provide extensive layerwise diagnostics and ablations for drift correction, residual compensation, attention weighting, and adaptive mixing.

Presentation: The motivation, theoretical development, practical modifications, and limitations are generally organized clearly. The authors appropriately acknowledge the absence of throughput measurements, the restricted model scale, and the layerwise Euclidean objective.

Reproducibility and ethics: Calibration data construction, principal hyperparameters, rate-search procedure, side-information accounting, and model-specific interventions are described in considerable detail. The work poses no apparent material ethical concern, and the stated limitations are candid.
weaknesses: The near-optimality claim is considerably narrower than the title and some summary language suggest. It applies asymptotically at high rate and large output dimension, assumes i.i.d. Gaussian weight rows, and analyzes PlainWaterSIC rather than the full practical pipeline. The asserted uniformity over all PSD covariances also needs qualification because the derivation uses positive Cholesky diagonals, determinants, and inverses and does not clearly handle singular covariance matrices.

The main rate comparisons mix entropy estimates for WaterSIC with log-cardinality rates for several baselines. Table 6 shows that actual Zstandard/LZMA storage exceeds entropy by roughly 0.04-0.20 bits per parameter, but this check covers only 14 matrices from two layers at one target rate. Reporting complete serialized model sizes, including codec and metadata overhead, could alter close frontier comparisons.

The practical gains cannot be cleanly attributed to waterfilling. The full method combines unequal rates with LMMSE reconstruction, activation-drift and residual corrections, diagonal rescaling, attention weighting, adaptive per-layer searches, dead-feature removal, and model-specific outlier handling. Ablations mostly report layerwise MSE at 4 bits rather than end-task rate-perplexity frontiers for PlainWaterSIC versus each successive addition.

Generality is weakened by manually zeroing four specifically identified Qwen3-8B rows and corresponding columns. Although the authors report less than 0.01 perplexity change, this model-specific intervention is not part of a general automated rule and complicates comparisons with untouched baselines.

The empirical study relies heavily on WikiText-2 for both calibration and primary evaluation, provides no uncertainty or sensitivity across calibration samples/seeds, and does not evaluate perplexity on additional corpora. The downstream tables help, but several Qwen3-8B advantages over Huffman-GPTQ are mixed rather than uniformly favorable.

Reproducibility remains incomplete without released code or precise checkpoint identifiers, software/evaluation-harness versions, random seeds, hardware requirements, runtime, and quantization cost. The numerous per-layer searches over the full WikiText-2 training split may be expensive. Algorithm 3 also contains inconsistent i/k subscripts that should be corrected.

The lack of end-to-end decompression and inference measurements limits the practical claim: compressed storage rate does not by itself demonstrate deployable memory-bandwidth or latency improvements. Overall, the work is technically promising and useful, but these scope and validation gaps favor a weak accept rather than a full accept.

strengths: Originality: The paper makes a compelling connection between Gaussian rate-distortion theory, predictive coding, and GPTQ. The resulting inverse-Cholesky-diagonal allocation is a simple, interpretable modification rather than an opaque heuristic.

Soundness: Under the stated high-rate i.i.d.-Gaussian model, the analysis clearly identifies the AM-GM penalty incurred by equal-spacing entropy-coded GPTQ and derives the asymptotic 0.255-bit scalar-quantization gap for PlainWaterSIC. The proof appendices are substantive.

Significance: The empirical improvements are often large, especially below 3 bits, and are demonstrated across Llama-2/3/3.2, Qwen3, and a 70B model. C4 and zero-shot evaluations substantially strengthen the evidence beyond WikiText-2 perplexity alone.

Evaluation: The manuscript includes useful studies of calibration-domain shift, context length, actual Zstandard/LZMA compression, weight Gaussianity, and several practical corrections. Reporting both WaterSIC and WaterSIC-FT helps separate quantization from subsequent tuning.

Presentation and reproducibility: The central intuition and algorithms are generally clear, while the appendices provide calibration procedures, optimizer settings, damping, rate matching, and other implementation details.
weaknesses: Soundness/claim scope: The advertised uniform 0.255-bit gap over all covariance matrices is not established as stated. Theorem 3.3 is a sequential asymptotic result as distortion tends to zero and the number of rows tends to infinity, under i.i.d. Gaussian weights. It does not establish a finite-rate guarantee at the experimentally emphasized 1–4 bits, nor uniform convergence over covariance matrices. Singular PSD covariances also invalidate expressions involving nonzero Cholesky diagonals, determinants, and the high-rate condition, despite the theorem claiming any PSD matrix.

The full practical WaterSIC contains many additions—LMMSE correction, drift and residual correction, attention weighting, per-layer adaptive searches, dead-feature removal, and rescaler optimization—that are outside the near-optimality theorem. Consequently, the theory does not directly support the performance or optimality claims for the evaluated algorithm and real LLM weights.

The state-of-the-art claim is overstated. At 2 bits, Table 10 reports PV-Tuning at 6.99 versus WaterSIC-FT at 7.20 on Llama-3-8B, and Table 13 reports 5.84 versus 5.86 on Llama-2-7B. Comparisons also mix entropy rates for WaterSIC with log-cardinality rates for several baselines; Table 6 shows that actual codecs can require roughly 0.05–0.2 additional bits per weight, which can matter in close comparisons.

The component ablations primarily show graphical layer-input MSE at 4 bits. They do not provide an additive numerical ablation on perplexity or downstream accuracy, making it difficult to determine how much of the gain comes from unequal rate allocation—the claimed main innovation—rather than the numerous auxiliary corrections and per-layer searches.

There are reporting inconsistencies: Llama-3.2-1B WaterSIC-FT at 1 bit is 30.47 in Table 1 but 32.85 in Tables 7 and 16, while the BF16 reference is variously 9.76 and 9.73. Algorithm 3 also contains index inconsistencies such as using z_k and gamma_k inside the loop over i. These should be resolved before publication.

Reproducibility remains incomplete. The PDF says code is available “here,” but no usable link is present. Random seeds or uncertainty, exact evaluation-harness settings, quantization/search runtime, and end-to-end artifact-size accounting are not reported. The expensive nested per-layer searches and hand-specified removal of particular Qwen rows further complicate independent reproduction and baseline comparability.

Practical significance is limited by the absence of end-to-end decompression throughput, memory-bandwidth measurements, or inference kernels. Thus, the work establishes compression-quality improvements but not that the variable-length representation yields deployable speed or memory benefits on current hardware.

Ethics and limitations: No acute ethical issue is apparent, and the limitations section appropriately acknowledges missing hardware evaluation. However, the impact statement is boilerplate and does not discuss energy/access benefits, possible workload shifts from decompression, or broader deployment implications.

strengths: The paper develops a thoughtful information-theoretic perspective on layerwise weight quantization. Under its stated i.i.d. Gaussian-weight, positive-definite covariance, high-rate, and large-output-dimension regime, the waterfilling connection and the 0.255-bit scalar-lattice gap are interesting and reasonably well motivated.

The practical method is more than a superficial application of the theory: it includes unequal per-column rates, activation-drift and residual-stream corrections, attention-weighted calibration, dead-feature handling, and row/column rescaling.

The empirical results are extensive. Appendices evaluate five model sizes/families, including Llama-3-70B, over 1–4 bits, and report WikiText-2, C4, KL divergence, and multiple zero-shot tasks. The reported low-bit improvements over Huffman-GPTQ are often large.

The manuscript includes useful ablations for residual correction, activation-drift correction, attention weighting, and adaptive mixing, as well as calibration-corpus and context-length sensitivity studies.

Reproducibility is helped by pseudocode, calibration construction, optimizer settings, damping values, rate-search details, and side-information accounting. The limitations section appropriately acknowledges the absence of hardware-throughput evaluation and possible scaling bottlenecks.
The societal risk appears limited for a model-compression method, and no material research-ethics concern is apparent.
weaknesses: The headline near-optimality claim is substantially broader than the theorem supports. The 0.255-bit result concerns PlainWaterSIC for i.i.d. Gaussian random weights, asymptotically high rate/low distortion and infinitely many independent rows. Actual LLM weights are deterministic and visibly non-Gaussian, practical rates are as low as 1–4 bits, and the evaluated full WaterSIC contains several heuristic corrections absent from the theorem. Thus the theory does not establish near-optimality of the practical method or of LLM quantization generally.

The asserted uniformity over all covariance matrices is not justified as written. The theorem states positive semidefinite covariance, but the construction and proof use nonzero Cholesky diagonals, inverses, a positive determinant, and strictly positive lattice spacings; singular PSD matrices violate these assumptions. Near-singular covariances are also precisely what motivate the paper's empirical dead-feature heuristic.

Rate comparisons are not fully commensurate or deployment-level. WaterSIC is generally plotted at empirical Shannon entropy, several competitors use log-cardinality, and Table 6 shows actual Zstandard/LZMA files exceeding entropy by roughly 0.04–0.20 bits/weight on selected layers. No complete serialized-model size, decoder representation, random-access cost, inference kernel, decompression throughput, or latency is evaluated. Consequently, claims about compressed model size and state-of-the-art practical compression are not established by the reported entropy frontier alone.

Several key gains come from a complicated collection of heuristics and expensive per-layer searches rather than the proposed waterfilling allocation alone. The ablations report intermediate activation MSE rather than end-task perplexity and do not isolate unequal-rate WaterSIC against an otherwise identical equal-rate method. The empirical evidence therefore does not clearly attribute the final SOTA results to the central theoretical innovation.

Baseline comparisons are partly imported from prior papers and use differing accounting conventions, contexts, calibration procedures, and fine-tuning status. WaterSIC-FT is sometimes highlighted against non-fine-tuned PTQ methods, making the broad SOTA language stronger than the controlled evidence warrants.

The Qwen3-8B pipeline manually zeros four model-specific outlier rows after checking that doing so changes WikiText-2 test perplexity by less than 0.01. This is test-set-informed method selection and a model-specific intervention not represented in the generic algorithm, weakening the fairness and reproducibility of those results.

Presentation contains consequential inconsistencies and typographical errors: the introduction describes spacing as proportional to conditional standard deviation whereas Eq. 12 uses its inverse; Appendix A adds zA to an integer-valued ZSIC output; and Algorithm 3 inconsistently switches between loop indices i and k. These ambiguities make independent implementation less reliable.

The PDF states that code is available “here,” but the supplied manuscript contains no functional link. Despite substantial appendix detail, the absence of accessible code, exact baseline artifacts, wall-clock quantization costs, memory requirements, and randomness reporting limits reproducibility.

The impact statement is generic rather than discussing practical concerns such as energy benefits versus the computational cost of calibration/fine-tuning, or the possibility that compression-induced accuracy degradation is uneven across tasks. This is not a decisive ethical defect, but it is underdeveloped.

strengths: Soundness: The paper develops a coherent connection between predictive quantization, GPTQ/SIC, and reverse waterfilling. Under its stated Gaussian, high-rate, and large-output-dimension regime, the AM–GM argument clearly motivates the unequal per-column spacings and explains why entropy-coded GPTQ can be arbitrarily suboptimal.

Originality: Allocating rates according to Cholesky innovation variances is a simple and apparently novel insight for LLM post-training quantization. The work contributes useful understanding in addition to an algorithm.

Significance: Results cover Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-2/3-7B/8B, Qwen3-8B, and Llama-3-70B across roughly 1–4 bits. WaterSIC generally improves perplexity over strong baselines, with especially large gains over Huffman-GPTQ at low rates; downstream zero-shot evaluations support that these gains are not confined to layerwise MSE.

The experiments include useful checks beyond the main WikiText-2 results: C4 evaluation, calibration/finetuning corpus sensitivity, context-length sensitivity, KL divergence, codec measurements, weight-distribution diagnostics, and component-level ablations.

Presentation: The central intuition is explained well, the algorithm is given in substantial detail, and the appendices document calibration, adaptive mixing, finetuning, rate control, and side-information accounting.

The limitations section appropriately acknowledges the absence of hardware throughput measurements and the mismatch between the layerwise objective and end-task loss. The work raises no evident material ethical concern; reducing model-storage requirements is broadly beneficial, although the impact statement is generic.
weaknesses: Soundness: The headline “uniformly over all covariance matrices” and 0.255-bit claim are overstated. Theorem 3.3 is an asymptotic high-rate result after taking the output dimension to infinity, assumes i.i.d. Gaussian weights, and effectively requires a positive-definite covariance. For singular PSD matrices, the Cholesky diagonal divisions and determinant-based high-rate formula are undefined or degenerate. The theorem should be restricted accordingly, with finite-rate behavior characterized separately.

The proof contains an apparent sign error in Eqs. (41), (42), and (57): high-resolution entropy behaves as H(round(V/α)) + log α → h(V), whereas the manuscript writes H−log α. As written, these displayed limits diverge. This may be repairable, but it prevents the current proof from being formally correct.

The theorem applies to PlainWaterSIC, while the strongest empirical system adds drift and residual corrections, attention-weighted calibration, per-layer searches, dead-feature erasure, row/column rescaling, model-specific interventions, and sometimes finetuning. Consequently, the theory does not establish near-optimality of the evaluated full algorithm, and the paper does not isolate end-to-end perplexity gains from the core waterfilling allocation versus these additional heuristics.

The bitrate comparison is not fully apples-to-apples: WaterSIC often reports ideal empirical entropy, while several baselines use log-cardinality. Table 6 shows actual Zstd/LZMA sizes can exceed entropy by approximately 0.02–0.20 bits/weight on selected layers, but complete-model codec sizes are not used for the main frontiers. Decoder metadata, file-format overhead, random access, decompression latency, and inference throughput are not evaluated.

Several empirical inconsistencies need resolution. For Llama-3.2-1B at one bit, Table 1 reports WaterSIC-FT perplexity 30.47 and BF16 9.76, whereas Table 7 reports 32.85 and 9.73 under seemingly similar settings. The manuscript also alternates between calling WikiText-2 evaluation “validation” and “test.” Baseline results are partly imported from prior work, so exact preprocessing and evaluation equivalence should be demonstrated more carefully.

Reproducibility is only moderate despite detailed pseudocode. The manuscript lacks runtimes and compute costs for the expensive per-layer coordinate searches, random seeds or variability, software versions, a precise deployable codec/decoder specification, and complete-model compressed sizes. The code link is not concretely accessible in the provided manuscript. Algorithm 3 also contains index inconsistencies such as using z_k and γ_k inside an i-loop.

Presentation needs polishing: there are numerous typographical/indexing errors, some claims are broader than the supporting conditions, and several dense ablation plots are difficult to read. The ablations report mainly activation MSE at four bits rather than perplexity across rates, which limits their evidential value.

The practical significance remains uncertain because the proposed variable-length entropy representation may trade storage for substantial decoding and kernel complexity. Until end-to-end memory, latency, and throughput are reported, claims of deployment-relevant state of the art should be qualified. Overall, the conceptual and empirical merits support a weak accept, but the theorem statement/proof and rate-accounting issues prevent a stronger rating.
